## Voice-note transcription (round 2 item 3) — H1 fix, final handoff #2

**Branch:** cmd/workspace-00029-bs17. Prior candidate 417e6cd was reviewed (session 4d1c8a10) and returned NOT CLEARED: 0 critical / 1 HIGH (blocking) / 1 medium (docs) / 1 low (docs). New candidate/head SHA: ccc35261c54a82643e101a6c6ef6cc42c81f3a4d.

**H1 fix (blocking):** cmd can legitimately return a JSON body whose `text` field decodes, via `response.json()`, into a Python string holding an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate (the plain ASCII escape u+d800, no malformed JSON needed). Storing that string crashed SQLite's text bind with UnicodeEncodeError, which `_record()`'s catch-all swallowed by design, leaving the row `pending` forever — an infinite spinner, no error, no Retry, until the process happened to restart. Fixed in `_parse_success` (wixy_server/livechat/transcribe.py): the text is now checked via a UTF-8 encode round-trip and, if it contains a lone surrogate, mapped to the existing `TranscribeResult("invalid")` outcome — the same clean failed/invalid_response path the >200,000-char guard already used (working Retry button, no stuck spinner). Proven: (1) a red-first client-level test built from raw poisoned wire bytes, confirmed to crash with UnicodeEncodeError before the fix and pass after; (2) a full end-to-end route-level test (fake transport actually returning the poisoned bytes through the real route+job+store pipeline) confirming the row lands failed, the wire never carries the text, and a second Retry against the same poisoned transport still fails cleanly rather than crashing; (3) mutation-checked — the guard line removed, both new tests fail, restored.

**M1 (docs, non-blocking):** decisions/00167 item 5's wording on the rate limiter vs the concurrency limiter rewritten for clarity — they are two independent, non-conflicting gates (6/min-per-identity REFUSES at accept time; the CapacityLimiter(1) only ever QUEUES an already-accepted job, never refuses).

**L1 (docs, non-blocking):** added a docstring note on fake_cmd.py's transcribe double explaining it doesn't itself reject a missing private=1/cleanup=0 or a session_id/context field, and why that's not a live gap (CmdTranscriber.transcribe's own signature has no parameter to send them through).

**Also rebased onto current main** (which had moved past c55e8ba): a real merge conflict in admin-ui/src/server/thread.ts (main's send-flicker/composer-focus fixes landing in the same file as my transcript in-place-patch logic) resolved cleanly by git's auto-merge, verified by reading the result; docs/ai/testing.md and the generated bundle also conflicted, resolved by hand and full rebuild from the merged, typechecked source respectively. Confirmed both branches' features are present in the rebuilt bundle (wx-srv-transcript classes AND the new tap-precision/composer-focus code) and their e2e specs (server-transcription + server-tap-precision + server-send-no-flicker + server-composer-focus) run together against one shared fixture chat with zero interference: 25/25 passed.

**Fresh full verification after the merge:** backend pytest 1909/1909 (was 1906 before the two new surrogate tests); ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy strict clean; admin-ui typecheck clean; admin-ui vitest 1377/1377 (was 1358, plus 19 from main's own new gesture/settings tests); npm run build -> zero drift after rebuild. Every new/changed guard mutation-checked.

Self-review: 0 remaining critical/high. Ready for re-review by session 4d1c8a10 (does H1 hold fixed?) and your own mechanical verification.

## Round 2 item 4: per-device "Keep this device unlocked" + the two lock checkboxes — FINAL

**Branch:** `cmd/workspace-00029-bs15` · **Head SHA:** `fe9b63796c7c5e31b5a89a97255a6a07de61e3b3` · **Base:** `origin/main` (merged at `1406c3c`, which includes upstream round-2 items 1/5/6 through `b74cf7d`)

### What shipped this round

1. Merged `origin/main` (double-tap-to-lock SAME PLACE/SAME THING fix, send-no-flicker, composer-focus) — resolved 4 conflicts (panel.ts multi-tap wiring, docs/ai/testing.md, the admin bundle) and fixed 12 test call-sites across `gestures.test.ts` and `panelGrant.test.ts` that used the pre-fix tap-recognizer API (pointerdown-only instead of pointerdown+pointerup pairs).
2. Applied the independent opus reviewer's + Architect's round-2b fixes (already committed by my predecessor, `e123deb`): pause-at-shield-time, `shieldTainted`, the causal screen-lock evidence window (§8 ruling), only-`grant_invalid` clears the grant, `disposed` teardown guard, `idleAway`, 30s renewal retry, retry-on-visible, proof cleared without a detector — plus the `panelGrant.test.ts` test suite for all of it (110→178 tests).
3. Settings-sheet accessibility: `aria-describedby` links each checkbox to its explanatory note, `role="status"` on every dynamic note, and a new note under the greyed auto-lock row ("Off — nothing to extend while this device is kept unlocked").
4. Fixed a real e2e regression found by running the full `server-*.spec.ts` suite for the first time this round: the auto-lock row lacked its own CSS class (unlike its 3 siblings), so `.wx-srv-sheet-idle` resolved to 4 elements and Playwright's strict mode threw. Gave it `wx-srv-sheet-idle-row`.
5. Docs: `docs/ai/livechat.md` §15, `invariants.md` Inv 42, `glossary.md`, `decisions/00161` all updated to describe the causal-evidence rule, taint, pause timing, etc.
6. Mutation testing on the round-2b fixes found one real gap (nothing proved `beginShield()`'s taint reset mattered) — added the missing test — and 3 provably-equivalent survivors, each proved equivalent and documented in `scratch/mutate_frontend.py` + `decisions/00161`.

### Verification (all green on `fe9b637`)

- Backend: `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy` (211 files) — clean. Backend Python untouched this round; full `pytest` (1970 passed) was verified pre-merge on `5718ec1` and no backend file changed since (confirmed via `git diff --stat` against the merge base).
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npx vitest run` — **1844 passed**, 73 files. Bundle rebuilt, second build is a byte-for-byte no-op (zero drift).
- Frontend mutation testing (`scratch/mutate_frontend.py`, 90 mutants covering `lockModel.ts`/`panel.ts`/`deviceGrant.ts`/`api/grants.ts`/`settingsSheet.ts`/`screenWatcher.ts`/`lockSettings.ts`/`pinPad.ts`/`gestures.ts`): **87 killed, 3 documented equivalent mutants** (proved, not just asserted — see decisions/00161 "Round 2b" section), 0 skips.
- E2E (Playwright, real browser, all 10 `server-*.spec.ts` files, 128 tests): **128/128 passed** in 4.5 min, including the newly-added `server-tap-precision.spec.ts` and `server-send-no-flicker.spec.ts` from the merge.

### Deviations from the original brief

- The fallback when the browser cannot distinguish a screen lock from a tab switch is "lock if EITHER box is ticked", not "follow the tab box" (spec §8 literal wording) — documented in decisions/00161, approved by the Architect's earlier ruling.
- A transient renewal failure now retries every 30s instead of locking on the first failure — found necessary while fixing the reviewer's MEDIUM finding on 401 handling, not in the original brief.
- The auto-lock row gained its own CSS class (`wx-srv-sheet-idle-row`) — a pure implementation fix, no behavioural change, needed because the row was one of 4 sharing a class with no way to select it alone.

### Known limits (unchanged from earlier rounds)

- **On-device Android timing is UNVERIFIED** — needs the operator's phone. The design fails closed without it: an unproven device keeps locking on every background switch. This is the single most important thing for the operator to know before relying on the feature on his own phone.
- PIN rotation does not revoke device grants (documented in the runbook: use "Sign out other devices").
- Migration v7 (`device_grants` table) is provisional — `_LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` may need renumbering if another round-2 item's migration lands first; the store tests import the constant so a renumber is a one-line change.

Every medium/low finding from the independent opus reviewer and the Architect's ruling has been implemented, tested (unit + mutation + e2e), and documented. No open findings. The 3 mutation-test survivors are proved-equivalent, not overlooked — each has a one-paragraph proof in `decisions/00161`.

tasks.title: BUG: input box loses focus after Send

tasks.evidence_md: Merged as PR #254 -> main 9718099 (squash, Release-note trailer; rebased on 8fe7007 first so CI ran on the combined result). Root cause: send() calls composer.setBusy(true), which disables the textarea; disabling a focused element drops its focus and re-enabling never restores it. Fix: restoreComposerFocus() in thread.ts after the send settles (success after reset, failed result, thrown error), only while focus is lost (body) or on the composer's own controls, so it never steals focus the user moved elsewhere. tasks.title: BUG: double-tap-to-lock (R3) is too easily triggered by two unrelated taps in different places
tasks.detail_md: Operator report (round 2): rapid scrolling/tapping, or tapping two different menu items in quick succession, locks the chat as a false-positive panic lock. Root cause: gestures.ts's createMultiTapDetector counts ANY two primary-button pointerdowns within MULTI_TAP_INTERVAL_MS (400ms) of each other ANYWHERE in the panel - there is currently no spatial proximity check at all, only timing. Operator's own framing: it must require the two taps to land 'very much in the same place, quite quick'. This is the R3 panic/deliberate-lock mechanism (spec/server-chat/00-brief.md); item 4 (permanent unlock) pauses its grant on the SAME lock trigger, so this needs a coordinate/design ruling before I change the detector, not a unilateral tuning of the security-relevant threshold.
tasks.evidence_md: Merged as PR #258 -> main b74cf7d (squash), live (confirmed /api/version). Per Architect ruling R3 v1.7 (spec PR #256): a double-tap now needs a genuine TAP (down+up, <=10px, <=300ms, never pointercancel'd - shared with R2 decoy-reveal too), the SAME PLACE (<=32px of the run's first tap) and the SAME THING (same nearest interactive/bubble zone); a gesture-boundary tap closing a run started elsewhere stays exempt, unchanged. gestures.ts rewritten around a shared tap recognizer. Two real bugs in my own first pass caught by the existing unit suite going red (a boundary-closing regression; a boundary-chain counter reset by a shared helper), both fixed. Red-first: unit tests confirmed red with the gate forced open; a new mobile e2e spec (real touch events) confirmed red on the pre-fix bundle via stash-and-rerun. Full regression: vitest 1326/1326, 82/82 across every server e2e file, zero drift. Decision 00163.

tasks.title: FEATURE: reply to a specific message (quote-reply)
tasks.detail_md: Operator request (round 2, live, 2026-09-25 ~15:xx UK): "I need the ability to reply to a particular message." Read as: a quote-reply feature in the Server chat, same pattern as WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack - select a specific message and compose a reply that references it, with a quoted preview shown above the composer while typing and a compact quote header in the sent bubble linking back to the original. Scope as its own spec note in the ledger (do not retrofit through the general AI-chat component - decisions/00110's split keeps the two chat subsystems separate, same rule reactions followed). Suggested approach for consistency with the existing UI: add "Reply" as a new action in the existing message action menu (the same trigger that already has Copy and the reaction picker), rather than inventing a new gesture - avoids any interaction with the R3 double-tap-lock / R2 decoy-reveal gesture-boundary detectors. Needs: reply_to reference on the message model (nullable FK to another message in the same conversation; decide behavior when the target is later deleted - likely show a 'message deleted' placeholder rather than dropping the reference, matching the erasure invariants used elsewhere), API support on POST /messages, composer quoted-preview UI, sent-bubble quote header UI, tap-to-scroll-to-original. No new migration-version bump without checking current max (assigned at merge, take max+1, do not hard-code in spec text - same discipline as every schema-touching branch this round).

tasks.title: BUG: PIN pad number tap target too small (only the circle, not its square cell)
tasks.detail_md: Operator report (round 2, live, 2026-09-25): "when you are tapping the numbers for the pin number, it only triggers if you hit the circle but it should really trigger if you hit anywhere in the square that the circle sits within." tasks.evidence_md:
Merged as PR #260 -> main 7eee810 (squash, R14a Release-note trailer). Operator report: tapping near the edge of a PIN-pad digit did nothing. Root cause, measured live via Playwright: `border-radius:50%` on the key button clips Chromium's hit-testing to the inscribed circle, not the button's full 56/64px square layout cell -- corner offsets up to 6-8px silently missed (proven with a direct click-registration sweep, and confirmed causal by overriding border-radius to 0 and re-measuring, which restored full-square clicks). Fixed by drawing the circle via a `::before` pseudo-element (with its own stacking context via `z-index:0` on the button, so the pseudo doesn't escape behind the panel background -- a real regression I caught and fixed mid-investigation via a live screenshot comparison) while the button itself stays a plain square hit target.

Red-first: new e2e test clicking 2px inside a key's true corner, on both desktop and mobile viewports -- failed on the original code, passes after the fix. Full server-lock.spec.ts suite (40 tests) and the complete e2e suite (150 tests) pass; visually identical to the original (screenshot-compared pixel-for-pixel look).

My own independent mechanical verification: ruff/mypy clean, admin-ui typecheck clean, vitest 1366/1366, npm run build zero drift.

Live verified: /api/version reports 7eee810 (count 268) on both http://127.0.0.1:9380 (local blue slot) and https://ca.cinnamons.uk (public).

Note: this fix required two separate merge-conflict resolutions as items 2 (reactions) and 3 (transcription) landed on main while this PR was in flight -- both were mechanical (only generated bundle files conflicted, regenerated not hand-merged) and independently re-verified after each merge.
